title: Ported my WIP Roblox Cab game to ThreeJS with the gauntlet prompt
author: re-skob
selftext:
I ran Opus 5 through the Gauntlet prompt that's been going around to one-shot games. This wasn't a one-shot, I was working on this Crazy Taxi-inspired game Nutso CabO for Roblox a few months back and I figured I'd run it through to see how it does at a ThreeJS port of it. I ran out of Opus tokens part of the way through and let Sol crunch on it the rest of the way.  
  
Opus did all of the geometry from scratch based on the tools I had in the Roblox repo - a map generator, Blender based procedural building tool, and a GLB of the cab from Tripo, and it put together the rest and made all of the textures from scratch.  
  
The Roblox game is meant to be multiplayer and it ported the whole server and client side architecture but I haven't actually tested this multiplayer yet.  
  
Theme track is from Suno that I already had generated from when I was working on the Roblox version.

comments.author: mrbadface
comments.body: Doesnt /goal basically handle this all now? Or does it help to be explicit

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: not really because /goal uses itself as the decision maker if the job is done, whereas with the gauntlet prompt there are observer agents whose sole job is comparing screenshots side by side and judging whether the job is done and looping back around with their feedback. I saw a bunch of iterations that would have been approved but then got sent back after review
